intro: In Bursa province stands the Green Mosque, built in 1412–1419 as the mosque of Mehmed I's complex. Its royal loge tiles and its mihrab are reckoned the high point of early Ottoman decoration. Take your time here, and let the tiles speak.
history: The mosque of Mehmed I's complex at Bursa was finished in 1419. Its decoration was the work of tile masters from Tabriz, and the tiling of the royal loge and the mihrab is reckoned the high point of early Ottoman ornament. Its plan matters too: it is the most developed example of the inverted-T Bursa plan.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the royal loge, the tiled mihrab, the inverted-T plan and the portal.
facts: Did you know? The outside was never finished. The marble carving stops part way, and you can still see the masons' setting-out lines on the stone. Tile masters from Tabriz carried out the decoration, and the royal loge is the high point of early Ottoman ornament.
outro: This brings our journey through the Green Mosque to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
